title: Fixed Long Pendulum and Twin Anvil Impact Tester
description: One newly authored whole static pendulum-impact-tester-inspired exhibit. A broad chamfered sole supports two separate tall tapered cast standards with full rear buttresses and low tie, two proud bearing housings and a complete retained top crossshaft. A full long rectangular pendulum arm connects a round central hub to a complete chamfered lower hammer body with a short blunt nose, posed forward and above the empty low testing bay. Two full separated anvils sit on a low common seat with a real empty centre slot; no specimen is present. A whole side circular dial back, inset opaque face, complete pointer and nine uncalibrated raised radial markers are distinct from the weighted arm, with a small fixed hand brake lever at the opposite shaft end. A whole low rear stop bumper is rooted in the base. No clock escapement, toothed wheel, pallet, H-press upright, hydraulic ram or planishing C frame imported. Unlike the full forked-anchor clock display it has a single high bearing axis, a large long-arm hammer and independent low twin anvils rather than a tooth wheel and light rear bob; unlike the H press it has no tall pinned workbed or vertical sliding ram; unlike the planishing hammer it has no deep C frame, paired coaxial small dies, air head or control hose. One model zero scenes. Empty fixed illustrative display only, not an operable or safety-enclosed machine: no swing, release, impact, energy scale, test result, material strength, standards compliance, guard effectiveness, mechanical fit, load, manufacture or engineering/safety capability made or verified. Blunt geometry, no sharp specimen notch or test specimen. Rigging animation physics interaction not made.
